introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
10. (i) Air is escaping from a spherical balloon at the rate of $4\,\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$ at the instant when the radius is $2\,\text{cm}$.

Find,

a) in terms of $\pi$, the rate of decrease of the radius. *[3 marks]*

[Volume of a spherical balloon is $\dfrac43\pi r^3$ and Surface area is $4\pi r^2$]
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume is decreasing at $4\ \text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$, so $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-4$.

With $V=\dfrac43\pi r^3$: $\dfrac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$. By the chain rule,

$$\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}\;\Rightarrow\;-4=4\pi r^2\,\frac{dr}{dt}.$$

At $r=2$: $-4=16\pi\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=-\dfrac{1}{4\pi}$.

**Answer: the radius decreases at $\dfrac1{4\pi}\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$ ($\approx0.080$ cm s$^{-1}$).**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) the rate of decrease of the surface area of the spherical balloon. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$S=4\pi r^2$, so $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=8\pi r\,\dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

At $r=2$: $\dfrac{dS}{dt}=8\pi(2)\left(-\dfrac1{4\pi}\right)=-4$.

**Answer: the surface area decreases at $4\ \text{cm}^2\text{s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) The area of the finite region between the curve $y^2=4-x^2$, and the line $x=0$ and $x=2$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis. Find the volume generated. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis is $V=\pi\displaystyle\int_a^b y^2\,dx$. Here $y^2=4-x^2$ and the limits are $x=0$ to $x=2$:

$$V=\pi\int_0^2(4-x^2)\,dx=\pi\left[4x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\pi\left(8-\frac83\right)=\frac{16\pi}{3}.$$

(Check: the curve is the circle $x^2+y^2=4$, and the region rotates into a hemisphere of radius $2$, with volume $\frac12\cdot\frac43\pi(2)^3=\frac{16\pi}{3}$.)

**Answer: $V=\dfrac{16\pi}{3}\approx16.8$ cubic units.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) The position vectors of three particles of mass $2\,\text{kg}$, $3\,\text{kg}$ and $5\,\text{kg}$ are $(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)$, $(-3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)$ and $(2\mathbf i-5\mathbf j)$ respectively. Find the position vector of the centre of gravity of these particles. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The position vector of the centre of gravity is $\bar{\mathbf r}=\dfrac{\sum m_i\mathbf r_i}{\sum m_i}$.

Total mass: $2+3+5=10$ kg.

$$\sum m_i\mathbf r_i=2(2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j)+3(-3\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)+5(2\mathbf i-5\mathbf j)$$

$$=(4-9+10)\mathbf i+(6+12-25)\mathbf j=5\mathbf i-7\mathbf j.$$

Divide by $10$:

$$\bar{\mathbf r}=\frac{5\mathbf i-7\mathbf j}{10}=0.5\mathbf i-0.7\mathbf j.$$

**Answer: $\bar{\mathbf r}=0.5\mathbf i-0.7\mathbf j$.**
